newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco lawyers seek gag order on Miami lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco lawyers seek gag order on Miami lawyer.

text.p: Philp Morris Cos Inc. asked a judge to impose a gag order on Miami attorney Stanley Rosenblatt, who is scheduled to show excerpts from his depositions of tobacco company excutives on the CBS show 60 Minutes, the Miami Herald said on Saturday.
The gag order request was filed Friday and was scheduled to be heard Monday by Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye.

According to the Herald, Rosenblatt will appear Sunday on 60 Minutes and will air an excerpt of a deposition Rosenblatt conducted with Philip Morris President James Morgan. The newspaper said that in the deposition, Morgan compared cigarette addiction to a craving for Gummy Bears candies.
Rosenblatt represents airline flight attendants in a class-action lawsuit alleging that second-hand smoke made them sick.

Philp Morris asked that Rosenblatt be barred from conducting press conferences, granting interviews or making public comments about the evidence in the case, which is scheduled to go to trial in June.

"If ever there was a case which required 'muzzling,' it is this case," Philip Morris attorney Barry Davidson wrote in the request for a gag order. "The pervasive and inflammatory drumbeat of publicity and distribution of discovery material in this case is not appropriate and clearly is prejudicial."
Davidson indicated that significant portions of pre-trial depositions of tobacco company presidents have been widely disseminated and could prejudice potential jurors.
The Miami Herald recently ran a story quoting from transcripts of the depositions but did not say how it obtained them.
Neither Davidson nor Rosenblatt could be reached for comment Saturday.

Rosenblatt told the Herald that he had not called news conferences. He said news reporters sought him out for comment on tobacco-related issues because of his involvement in several lawsuits against the cigarette makers.
